subject: Discovery recap & PoC onboarding plan — FastRetail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & PoC onboarding plan — FastRetail

Hi Sam / Mia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before the PoC kickoff:

Pain points we heard
- Customer-facing recommendation generation is currently inconsistent and slow at peak (p95 latency ~450ms), which hurts conversions.
- Embedding-based semantic search is brittle; current pipeline is expensive to run at scale.
- Security/data residency concerns: product team needs to ensure PII is not sent to third-party SaaS without controls.

Current stack
- Backend: Node services on AWS (ECS + RDS).
- Inference: in-house LLM for generation + vector DB (managed) for embeddings.

Success criteria for the PoC
- Latency: p95 generation <200ms for typical user prompts
- Cost: demonstrable cost reduction per request (target: 30% reduction vs current infra)
- Quality: parity or better on 3 chosen evaluation prompts (will share eval prompts)
- Security: clear path for private deployment / VPC + KMS integration for PII-sensitive flows

Proposed PoC & onboarding plan (8 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff + env access and security questionnaire
- Week 1: auth, API keys, and network connectivity (VPC options) + install SDKs (Python/Node)
- Week 2: embeddings integration + vector DB proof points (endpoints + sample pipeline)
- Week 3: generation integration for recommendation flows (latency profiling)
- Week 4: tuning (batching/quantization) and cost optimization recommendations
- Week 5: end-to-end integration & smoke tests
- Week 6: run evaluation prompts, collect metrics and qualitative feedback
- Week 7: iterate on tuning and fallback policies
- Week 8: final review, success metrics, and next steps for production rollout

Owners
- FastRetail product owner: Sam Taylor
- Engineering lead (integration): Mia Lopez
- Redwood: Marissa (sales), Ben Carter (solutions engineer), Dev Patel (CSM)

Integration details we discussed
- SDKs: primary languages supported and recommended: Python (fastest path), Node (our reference), Java (partial support). We'll send language-specific examples.
- API compatibility: Our REST API and SDKs support streaming responses, structured JSON outputs, and function/tool calling. If you have a custom protocol we can map.
- Data handling: options for Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private (VPC). For PII-sensitive flows we recommend either Dedicated capacity with private networking or our Private deployment.

Attachments: PoC_Scope_v1.pdf (scope & milestones), redwood_sdk_matrix.xlsx (language feature matrix), security_checklist.pdf (initial security answers).

Next steps
- Sam / Mia: please confirm the PoC timeline and owners, and share the primary integration engineer for setup (Slack/Zoom handle).
- We'll schedule a kickoff for next week; proposed slot: Tue Aug 8 9:00–10:00am PT. Please let us know if that works.

I'll follow up with calendar invites and the onboarding checklist.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications before kickoff: 

1) Data residency: for the PII-sensitive recommendation use-case, we need logs to stay in our AWS account and for keys to be customer-managed (KMS/HSM). Which deployment option maps to that?

2) SDKs: our integration team is Node-first. Will the Node SDK support streaming responses and function/tool calling the same way the Python one does?

Confirmed owners: Sam (product), Mia (engineering lead). I'll loop in our infra lead (cc'ed) once we lock the kickoff.

We can do the Tue Aug 8 9am PT kickoff — Mia and I are available.

Cheers,
Sam Taylor

sam@fastretail.com

Hi Sam — great, thanks for the quick turn. Answers below and next steps: 

1) Data residency / KMS: For control over keys and log residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated or our Private deployment. Dedicated gives you isolated capacity and customer-managed KMS with VPC peering for logs; Private (on-prem/VPC) gives the strongest guarantees but requires a slightly longer onboarding window. For the PoC we can start on Dedicated with customer-managed KMS — that meets the requirement and keeps the timeline tight. Ben will follow up with the infra checklist for Dedicated.

2) Node SDK parity: Yes — Node SDK supports streaming responses and function/tool calling (same behavior as Python). We have a few small differences in helper utilities; the redwood_sdk_matrix.xlsx I attached shows feature parity and recommended patterns. Ben will share a short Node sample (streaming + function call) before kickoff.

Next steps:
- I'll send the calendar invite for Tue Aug 8 9:00am PT (invite includes Zoom + agenda).
- Ben: please attach the Dedicated infra checklist and a Node streaming example in this thread.
- Sam / Mia: please share the infra lead's contact for VPC setup (we'll need an IAM contact + network owner).

Attaching PoC_Scope_v1.pdf again.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
